topline.text: Another quiet 24-48 hours nationally - no new DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding, SEND or funding announcement cleared the corroboration bar, so today's edition stays short rather than padded.

The one live local story: NEU strike action at Talbot Specialist School in Norton Lees - a council-maintained SEND school - remains unresolved, with five further strike days called over workload, safety and governance concerns.
topline.action: Worth flagging to anyone who routes SEND placements or respite support through Talbot, in case further strike days this month disrupt provision.

topline.text: Reminder: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform closes in 8 days, on 19 November.

diary.text: Anti-Bullying Week 2026 - 'Break the Silence' theme; Odd Socks Day opens the week on 16 Nov.
DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes - 8 days away.
DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.

items.lede: Strike dispute continues at Sheffield SEND school.
items.body: NEU members at Talbot Specialist School, the Norton Lees school for pupils with SEND maintained directly by Sheffield City Council, walked out on 5 November citing 'excessive workload, safe working practices and a lack of transparency in school governance'. Five further strike days have been called over the following fortnight; the council says it has 'asked the NEU and its members... to reconsider their proposed action', with no resolution confirmed yet.
items.action: Worth flagging to any mainstream colleagues who route SEND placements or respite support through Talbot, in case further strike days this month disrupt provision.

box.quote: failing to engage in meaningful dialogue
box.author: Rafia Hussain, NEU Sheffield branch secretary, on the Talbot dispute
